\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادن} (mehmâni dâdan)}{مهمانی دادن (mehmâni dâdan)}]{\fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادن} (mehmâni dâdan) — to throw a party, to give a party}

\label{lesson:FA-C341-mehmani-dadan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a custom, then the Persian for wild rue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادن}}
\textbf{\fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادن}} (\emph{mehmâni dâdan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to throw a party, to give a party\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{تولد} \fa{خواهرم} \fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye tavallod-e khâharam mehmâni dâdim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We threw a party for my sister's birthday.
\end{quote}

Present \emph{mehmâni midahad}. \emph{Mehmâni raftan} is \textquotedblleft{}to go to a party\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mehmâni} \textquotedblleft{}a party\textquotedblright{} is built on \emph{mehmân} \textquotedblleft{}guest\textquotedblright{}, a native Persian word, and \emph{dâdan} \textquotedblleft{}to give\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian: to give a party.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mehmâni dâdan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mehmâni dâdan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{mehmâni dâdan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a custom, then the Persian for wild rue, then say \emph{mehmâni dâdan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{مهمانی} \fa{دادن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To throw a party, to give a party\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کردن} (pazirâyi kardan)}{پذیرایی کردن (pazirâyi kardan)}]{\fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کردن} (pazirâyi kardan) — to serve (guests), to entertain}

\label{lesson:FA-C341-pazirayi-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for wild rue, then the Persian for to throw a party.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{pazirâyi kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to serve (guests), to entertain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مادرم} \fa{با} \fa{چای} \fa{و} \fa{شیرینی} \fa{از} \fa{مهمانها} \fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Mâdaram bâ chây o shirini az mehmân-hâ pazirâyi kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother served the guests tea and pastries.
\end{quote}

The guests take \emph{az}. The noun \emph{pazirâyi} is also \textquotedblleft{}the living room\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{pazirâyi} \textquotedblleft{}reception\textquotedblright{} is built on \emph{pazir-}, the present stem of the native verb \emph{paziroftan} \textquotedblleft{}to receive\textquotedblright{}; \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian. EtymDB lists no entry.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pazirâyi kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pazirâyi kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{pazirâyi kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for wild rue, then the Persian for to throw a party, then say \emph{pazirâyi kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{پذیرایی} \fa{کردن} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To serve (guests), to entertain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کادو} (kâdo)}{کادو (kâdo)}]{\fa{کادو} (kâdo) — a present (everyday word)}

\label{lesson:FA-C341-kado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to throw a party, then the Persian for to serve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کادو}}
\textbf{\fa{کادو}} (\emph{kâdo}) — \textquotedblleft{}a present (everyday word)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برای} \fa{دوستم} \fa{یک} \fa{کادوی} \fa{کوچک} \fa{خریدم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâ-ye dustam yek kâdo-ye kuchak kharidam.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
I bought a small present for my friend.
\end{quote}

Everyday; \emph{hediye} is more formal. \emph{Kâdo kardan} is \textquotedblleft{}to gift-wrap\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kâdo} is borrowed from French \emph{cadeau}, \textquotedblleft{}gift\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kâdo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kâdo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to throw a party, then the Persian for to serve, then say \emph{kâdo} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{بادکنک} (bâdkonak)}{بادکنک (bâdkonak)}]{\fa{بادکنک} (bâdkonak) — a balloon}

\label{lesson:FA-C341-badkonak}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to serve, then the Persian for a present.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{بادکنک}}
\textbf{\fa{بادکنک}} (\emph{bâdkonak}) — \textquotedblleft{}a balloon\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{بچه} \fa{ها} \fa{با} \fa{بادکنک} \fa{بازی} \fa{میکردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Bachche-hâ bâ bâdkonak bâzi mikardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children were playing with balloons.
\end{quote}

\emph{bâd} \textquotedblleft{}wind, air\textquotedblright{} + \emph{kon-} \textquotedblleft{}make\textquotedblright{} + \emph{-ak}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{bâdkonak} is built from Persian \emph{bâd} \textquotedblleft{}wind, air\textquotedblright{}, \emph{kon-}, the present stem of \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to make\textquotedblright{}, and the suffix \emph{-ak}. All of it is native.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{شمع} (sham')}{شمع (sham')}]{\fa{شمع} (sham') — a candle}

\label{lesson:FA-C341-sham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a present, then the Persian for a balloon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{شمع}}
\textbf{\fa{شمع}} (\emph{sham'}) — \textquotedblleft{}a candle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{شمع} \fa{های} \fa{کیک} \fa{تولد} \fa{را} \fa{خاموش} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U sham'-hâ-ye keyk-e tavallod râ khâmush kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
She put out the candles on the birthday cake.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sham' roshan kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to light a candle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sham'} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{sham'}, \textquotedblleft{}wax, a candle\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
